subject: [PATCH v2] selftests: cover kernfs dentry revalidation

reviews.author: Christian Brauner
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that the patch has been applied to the vfs-7.4.kernfs branch and will appear in linux-next soon, but requested that any outstanding bugs be reported in a new review so the patch can be dropped.
reviews.raw_body:
Applied to the vfs-7.4.kernfs branch of the vfs/vfs.git tree.
Patches in the vfs-7.4.kernfs branch should appear in linux-next soon.

Please report any outstanding bugs that were missed during review in a
new review to the original patch series allowing us to drop it.

It's encouraged to provide Acked-bys and Reviewed-bys even though the
patch has now been applied. If possible patch trailers will be updated.

Note that commit hashes shown below are subject to change due to rebase,
trailer updates or similar. If in doubt, please check the listed branch.

tree:   https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/vfs/vfs.git
branch: vfs-7.4.kernfs

reviews.summary: Reviewer Christian Brauner requested shorter commit messages and changelogs, specifically mentioning that multi-paragraph descriptions are unwelcome in test commits.
reviews.raw_body:
I have to say I would appreciate trimmed-down commit messages with less
relative clauses. This reads very LLMy still. Especially for tests my
appetite for wading through multiple paragraphs of info is very low.
Same goes for the very wordy changelog below...

base on vfs branch. Just wanted to give a headsup.

Thanks a lot, Christian.

2026-09-04.patch_summary: This patch adds selftests to cover kernfs dentry revalidation, which is crucial for maintaining the integrity of the kernel's file system cache. The tests simulate various scenarios where the kernel modifies kernfs nodes without VFS calls, and verify that the dentry cache is correctly updated. This includes checking how cached negative and positive dentries are dropped when files appear or disappear, as well as testing concurrent lookups and operations across removals. The patch also ensures that walking dentries already in the cache does not cause them to be dropped. The tests cover both filesystems (cgroup2 and sysfs) and confirm that they catch a broken backstop by stubbing kernfs_dir_changed() to return false.

reviews.author: Christian Brauner
reviews.summary: Reviewer Christian Brauner asked to leave this patchset in the vfs tree, indicating no specific technical concerns or objections.
reviews.raw_body:
Ok, I've taken quite a few before not too long ago. Do you mind leaving
this set in the vfs tree?
